views.label: The same shape as matrix
views.note: Add element by element, multiply as a sum over k. The arithmetic has the shape of the real matrix.

views.label: Every product costs four
views.note: Each element product is a complex multiplication: four real multiplications and two additions.

views.label: Why not one module
views.note: One module for both would need a second copy of every function, or a check of the type inside every loop.

views.label: Who would pay for that
views.note: The caller who never uses a complex matrix is the common one on a small target, and would pay in size and speed.

boundaries.label: a separate module, for the cost it would otherwise add

cards.title: What it works out
items: (A * B)(i,j) = sum over k of A(i,k) * B(k,j)
Every one of those products is a complex multiplication

cards.title: What that costs
items: Four real multiplications and two additions for each element product
Thus a complex multiply costs about four times a real one of the same shape
That cost is the reason this is a module of its own

cards.title: Why not one module for both
items: It would need a second copy of each function, or a union and a type check in every loop
Both make the real matrix larger and slower
On a small target the caller who needs only real numbers is the common one
